[spoiler=[b]Conspirators[/b]

[i]The General and his men.[/i]]
A black SUV winds through the grid-like streets of Neudresden. Raindrops pour onto the windows, headlights slice into the night ahead. Due to the poor weather, heavy rainfall forecasted for the next week, scarcely many people are on the streets. 

At three in the morning the city felt dead. 

Only small groups of beggars can be seen, taking some rest before they are eventually shooed away by the Neudresden Polizei. Eventually, the car arrives before the Central Military Commission Offices in the Hauptstadt District. Its approach gradually slows as it nears the two guard booths that compose the entrance to the building. An officer steps out of his booth into the rain, eyeing the car wearily. 

Slowly the driver's side window rolls down. 

Identification.

The man reaches onto his dashboard and hands the officer several papers. His eyes flicker over the identification card. Then a sharp draw of breath comes as he reads the mans name.

Gen. Müller

He glances back up at the man in the car.

Without another word he retreats back into the booth to raise the barrier. 

The Central Military Commission Offices, like many of the other government buildings that populate the Haupstadt District had a storied history. Its neoclassical structure with large corinthian columns guarding the entrance, balustrade and elaborate reliefs had  nearly a century of Kaiserreich military history. Within the halls of the building the fate of Kaisers, countries, and entire peoples had been decided by the Reichswehr military machine. Now several men, Mr. Müller included, walk its halls on a seemingly unimportant rainy Monday night in a bid to completely change the Kaiserreich. 

The granite clinks under the General's shoes as he makes his way across the hallways. At the end of the hallway he opens a large pair of oak doors to find the other three men. Lieutenaut General Vogel, Vice Admiral Krause and General Keller all sat around the large circular table. 

Vogel rose and clasped Müllers hand firmly. Müller. Weve been waiting for you. 

Müller allowed a tight smile. Well Im here now gentlemen. Let's discuss business.

Müller tosses a small manila folder across the table towards the three other men. There's been talk of peace with the Hydronians.

He sips the water laid out before them on the desk before continuing. The Kaiser, Sturmfels and the rest of the Commission are out in Büdingen with WMW. We either act now or we wait another month.

Vogel nods his head as Müller speaks. We wait and we lose momentum. That dog Sturmfels and the Cyberverteidigung are already sniffing around the Armee. 

Krause shakes his head and lays down the folder. Nasty business. Peace. The Hochkaiser sells us out to the Bobians and now he asks for a deal with the Hydronians? Those disgusting sand-eaters attack us and then ask for peace? Jesus Christ.

Keller leans towards the General. Is the Fifth Armored with us? Müller, we need assurances. 

They are. But the Colonel is cautioustoo cautious.  

The room falls silent save for the ticking clock mounted on the back wall. 

Müller lights a cigarette. The light briefly illuminates his face before he exhales and speaks again. Ill speak with the Colonel. However, until then I expect everything we have discussed here to remain absolutely sealed.
 
The men nodded and rose. The meeting was over.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Back on the Warpath[/b]]

A total of three strike groups take off from Sturmfels and Bauer AFB both within Nestorstaat to begin suppression of enemy air defences. A total of eighteen J-16s act as the shooters of the strike groups, carrying a total of four REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles each on their pylons. Six EK-18 electronic warfare aircraft join the strike groups to provide offensive jamming capabilities. On top of this six J-15 air superiority aircraft escort the strike group to provide defense from the Enkian air force. Twelve strike aircraft join the strike groups carrying loadouts of JDAMs and SDBs. From behind two AWACs provide battle management while aerial refuelers pushed far behind enemy lines provide constant refueling. Multiple ISR drones also provide the strike groups with data on their targets. 

Falke-20 passive electronic warfare aircraft had for several weeks before the invasion started began analysis of Enkian transmissions. Antennas, sensors and receivers across its body and wings would maintain a constant interception of Enkian communications and signals. The data is sent via datalink to both forward bases in Nestorstaat and military centers in the Kaiserreich. Constant streams of data are analyzed by the Reichswehr to extract a wide range of information: the locations of air defenses that release signals to troops and asset movements relayed by the Enkians. 

Satellites do their job as well. The synthetic aperture radars aboard send pings onto the ground below to find air defense systems and relay their locations to the air force. Even under camouflage and other attempts at disguising the air defense the SAR would be quite effective at helping the Reichswehr to cut through and find the systems. 

Ground based tracing systems also aid the Reichswehr in finding the Enkian air defenses. Using ELINT, the Reichswehr both identifies and finds the locations of Enkian radar. L-bands help identify long-range radar, C-bands usually point out fire-control radars etc. On top of this multiple ground stations combined with the fourth fleet offshore would work together to triangulate the signals coming from the Enkian systems. 

By 0300 hours local time the bombardment would begin. 

The EK-18s first begin jamming the enemy's search radars to degrade their ability to track the incoming group of aircraft. Barrage jamming is used to hit a wide variety of frequencies to lower the signal-to-noise ratio and blind the Enkian radar. Ground based EW systems also provide deception coverage. By sending out false signals these systems create a variety of problems for the Enkians. Fake targets are created, the location of the incoming strike groups are moved and radars are saturated with misleading information. The EW aircraft also begin their usage of barrage jamming against Enkian communications to break down coordination and responses to the Reichswehr attack. 

The J-15 escort aircraft also come into play. From underneath their fuselages they launch TK-5 drones into Enkian airspace. Built to mimic the radar signature of J-16s and J-15s their purpose is to trigger Enkian air defense activation. The TK-5s are also equipped with their jamming capabilities which help the Reichswehr to continue its electronic warfare front. 

Targeting pods aboard the J-16s provide the last layer of identification before large scale kinetic strikes begin. They scan the area for radar emissions to detect and classify them for targeting by the strike group. This combined with degradation of the enemy's ability to respond, drone warfare, and previous intelligence gathering creates the conditions for the beginning of anti-radiation missile strikes. The first target is the fire-control radar of the Enkian military, the ones used to coordinate anti-air missile launches. REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles are fired into Enkian territory to destroy the air defenses. Their light weight and high speeds make them particularly hard to target for intercepting. The REG-3000 is able to reach supersonic speeds around mach 2 making the possibility of reacting in time extremely small. If radars are turned off the missile utilizes its LOAL capabilities backed by inertial navigation and GPS to continue its hunt.[/spoiler]

[nation]Technokratisches Kaiserreich[/nation][/quote]
The Guard Korps and the welcoming party lead the men into the Empfangshalle or the reception hall. Within the large, formal room they can spot a wide variety of both relics and goods. Large marble statues looted by Hochdeutsche crusaders from Shamat in the 700s can be seen in full display in the room. Along with the statue there are several large chairs where the men are seated while they wait, the imposing paintings of previous Hochkaisers and important figures in the Kaiserreichs history bearing down on them. At the end of the room stands a massive painting of the Battle of Selmyra, where the Kaiserreich had crushed the last Islamic emirate in Elseyr. 

After several minutes of waiting the large oak doors to the door open. Two members of the Guard Korps beckon the men forward into the Audienzsall. Lined with flags of the Kaiserreich and its provinces, natural sunlight flows through the large windows at either side of the room. At the end of the hall, Sturmfels sits behind his desk, quickly standing up and walking towards the group as they approach. 

I trust your journey was good Mr. Wolff?

[quote=roskesak;60063019][i][u][b]The Embassy Hostage Crisis
[/b][/u]
Smoke rolls above the rooftops. The crowds are gone. The only movement is that of the joint team of snipers, entrenched in their rooftop positions, awaiting the order.
KGI Commander was approached again by the two ISRP officers. One older, stoic, the other younger and serving as translator.

[b]KGI Commander
[/b] Youve already crossed the border with armed units and armored vehicles. Youd better explain who the hell authorized you.

The younger operative steps forward, showing a black enamel badge. 

[b]ISRP Translator[/b]
 We operate under the interlaw jurisdiction of international criminal enforcement. Were here to assist with the hostage embassy crisis.

You stiffen. That changes the calculus.  Interlaw jurisdiction gives them operational legitimacy barely, but your streets, your command still stands.

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 You track terrorists. I protect hostages. You can observe. You can advise. But this op remains under Roskeskan control.

The ISRP nods. No argument. Theyre trained for cooperation. The older operative pulls up a portable interface. It's already displaying live internal security feeds from the embassy, marked in Roskeskan. Your intel division mustve cracked the feeds minutes ago.

[b]ISRP Agent[/b]
 Two confirmed militants. First floor in the west hallway. One has a homemade explosive vest, likely a dead-man switch. Theyve barricaded the lobby and jammed some camera access. But not all.

Footage shows one is pacing with a rifle, the other glued to the windows*

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 The ISRP orders that we lure them in.

officers pause in confusion?*

[b]ISRP Agent[/b]
Make it look like we think there are more inside. Get loud. Shout false numbers. Act disorganized. Let them think were blind and paranoid.

You gesture to your rooftop units.

When the first pokes his head through the curtains, and drops him. Quietly. The second one will panic. Thats when we breach.

A joint special forces unit of KGI and ISRP sniper chimes in through the radio* 

Visual confirmation possible from roof 3A. Awaiting movement.

You nod. The trap is set.[/i][/quote]
The younger ISRP officer runs over to one of the vehicles and retrieves a loudspeaker, positioning himself in the middle of the street in front of the embassy. "WE KNOW YOU ARE IN THERE! WHAT ARE YOUR DEMANDS?"

A long minute passes waiting for a response, before a woman stumbles out the front door of the embassy, her hands up and a piece of paper in her right hand. The younger officer motions for her to walk forward and she does slowly, reaching the police line and being rushed to a nearby hospital to ensure she doesn't have any injuries. The translator takes the note and hands it to the KGI commander, letting him read it aloud.

"We demand the immediate release of all land illegally held by Roskesak and the command goes on to read most of the demand, muttering the words to himself before looking up and shaking his head. They are asking for something completely unreasonable. We cant accept this if we wanted to. 

The older ISRP officer heard something on his radio and listened to it, before saying something to his younger compatriot. Are your men ready to breach? the translator asks.

The commander takes a second to radio his men before responding Yes. The translator nods to the older man, prompting him to say something on the radio.

Unbeknownst to the commander, the ISRP men had located what they estimated to be all of the suspects, with only one of them anywhere near the hostages. One had even decided to try to peek out a window to see what they were dealing with, and that was all that was needed. An earsplitting boom rings out from a rooftop as a 13.2mm bullet shatters the window and kills the terrorist instantly. ISRP and KGI forces quickly breach the building and begin sweeping the halls and rooms of the embassy.
